title: 05_severe_phase_portrait_co_svr
interpretation: Severe sepsis (severity 3) plotted as a path in cardiac-output x vascular-resistance space rather than as two separate time series. Dots mark 6-hour intervals; the square is the shared healthy baseline (t=0), the stars are the 72 h endpoints, and grey dashes are iso-MAP contours (MAP = 17.34 x CO x SVR — a relation that holds to <0.5% in BOTH arms with the same constant). Both arms begin at the same point and finish below the MAP<65 shock contour (engine ~64 vs extraction ~58 mmHg — both now across the <65 threshold by 72 h, the extraction ~15 h earlier), but by orthogonal routes: the real BioGears engine slides LEFT — cardiac output fails 5.8->4.0 L/min while SVR stays flat (cold, low-output decline) — whereas the SBML extraction slides DOWN — it holds/rebuilds output and lets SVR swing up then fall to 0.60 (warm, vasodilatory decline). The orthogonality is the finding: the extraction's single AIR->sympathetic arc overshoots the vasomotor axis that the engine's full cardiovascular control keeps muted, so the two cross into MAP<65 shock by physiologically different routes. This is the geometric view of studies 03/05.
